Let \(m=n/2=2q^2\), the number of transposition blocks of \(\pi\).  
The required number of \(\widetilde C_\pi\)-conjugacy orbits is

\[
\boxed{\ell(\ell-1)^{r-2}(\ell^r-1)(\ell^{r-1}-1)}.
\]

Here is the derivation.

For \(\sigma\in\Gamma\) with \(\pi_\sigma=\pi\), write

\[
\sigma(\rho_j)=\zeta^{c_j}\rho_j,\qquad c_j\in\mathbb F_\ell^\times,
\]

and

\[
\sigma(\alpha_i^{(j)})=\zeta^{a_i^{(j)}}\alpha_{\pi(i)}^{(j)}.
\]

For a transposition block \(B=\{i,\pi(i)\}\), define

\[
S_B=(a_i^{(1)}+a_{\pi(i)}^{(1)},\dots,a_i^{(r)}+a_{\pi(i)}^{(r)})\in\mathbb F_\ell^r.
\]

The Kummer relation hypothesis implies that, up to \(\widetilde C_\pi\)-conjugacy, only the multiset of the \(S_B\)’s matters, together with \(c=(c_1,\dots,c_r)\). Since every \(c_j\ne0\), rescale coordinates and put

\[
x_B=\frac{S_B}{2c}\in\mathbb F_\ell^r.
\]

Let \(f(x)\) be the multiplicity of \(x\) among the \(x_B\)’s. Then

\[
\sum_x f(x)=m=2q^2.
\]

For \(k\in\mathbb F_\ell^r\), the number of \(2\)-cycles on \(\Omega_k\) is

\[
C(k)=\ell^r\left(2\sum_x f(x)f(x+k)-m\delta_{k,0}\right).
\]

The stated differences therefore force the autocorrelation

\[
A(k):=2\sum_x f(x)f(x+k)-m\delta_{k,0}
\]

to have three levels on a flag

\[
W\subset U\subset\mathbb F_\ell^r,\qquad \operatorname{codim}U=1,\quad \operatorname{codim}W=2,
\]

with

\[
A_W-A_U=8\ell^2(q+Q),\qquad A_U-A_O=8\ell(q+3Q).
\]

Fourier transforming, the corresponding Fourier magnitudes are

\[
|\widehat f(\chi)|=
\begin{cases}
q+4Q, & \chi\in U^\perp\setminus\{0\},\\
q+2Q, & \chi\in W^\perp\setminus U^\perp,\\
q, & \chi\notin W^\perp.
\end{cases}
\]

Because \(2\) generates \(\mathbb F_\ell^\times\), the primes \(q,q+2Q,q+4Q\) are inert in the \(\ell\)-cyclotomic field; hence each nonzero Fourier coefficient is forced to be that prime times a root of unity. The integrality and nonnegativity of \(f\) then force the common phase form, giving exactly one multiplicity function for each translate \(y\) and flag:

\[
f(x)=dq-4+2\ell\,1_{x-y\in U}+2\ell^2\,1_{x-y\in W}+q\,1_{x=y},
\]

where

\[
d=\frac{2q-1}{Q}.
\]

The relations for \(j<r\) impose

\[
\sum_x f(x)x_j=0\qquad (1\le j<r),
\]

so the translate \(y\) must have first \(r-1\) coordinates zero. Thus there are exactly \(\ell\) choices for \(y\).

Now count choices:

- \(c\in(\mathbb F_\ell^\times)^r\): \((\ell-1)^r\) choices.
- Flags \(W\subset U\subset\mathbb F_\ell^r\):

\[
\frac{\ell^r-1}{\ell-1}\cdot \frac{\ell^{r-1}-1}{\ell-1}.
\]

- Allowed translates \(y\): \(\ell\) choices.

Therefore the number of \(\widetilde C_\pi\)-conjugacy orbits is

\[
(\ell-1)^r\cdot \ell\cdot
\frac{\ell^r-1}{\ell-1}\cdot
\frac{\ell^{r-1}-1}{\ell-1}
=
\boxed{\ell(\ell-1)^{r-2}(\ell^r-1)(\ell^{r-1}-1)}.
\]
